features.description: Open-source browser control surface for agentic work: manage conversations, files, terminals, model configuration, backends and automations in one place.
Conversation view where OpenHands explains its actions.
Shows the file changes performed by OpenHands.
Browse and modify workspace files in an embedded VS Code; also used to upload and download files.
Shared space where OpenHands and the user run terminal commands.
Displays the web server when OpenHands runs an application so users can interact with it.
Non-interactive browser used by OpenHands to browse websites.
Automated web page interaction for agents, built on browser control.
Record and replay agent browser sessions with rrweb.
Run the agent server in isolated Docker containers for security and reproducibility; also Apptainer (rootless, HPC) and API-based hosted sandboxes.
Local, remote Agent Server, OpenHands Cloud, DigitalOcean Managed Agents, VM/self-hosted, per-conversation Docker, Kubernetes (Helm) and Modal backends.
Hosted cloud version at app.all-hands.dev with sandboxed conversations.
Install OpenHands Cloud for GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket repositories and work on them via the Cloud UI or the platform.
OpenHands Slack app for working with repos from Slack.
Jira integration with service account, API token and webhook configuration.
Programmatically start and monitor conversations, read files, get git changes and export trajectories.
Connect any LiteLLM-supported LLM: OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Azure, Gemini/Vertex, Groq, OpenRouter, Moonshot, DigitalOcean, LiteLLM proxy and the OpenHands provider.
Connect local servers such as LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM and SGLang.
Save model configurations and switch models mid-conversation via saved LLM profiles.
Confirmation policies (e.g. AlwaysConfirm) control when actions need user approval; pluggable security analyzers evaluate action risk.

Reusable instructions, domain knowledge and workflows: repo-level skills, keyword-triggered skills, deterministic path-triggered rules, org/user skills and a global registry (github.com/OpenHands/extensions).
A .openhands directory at the repo root customizes skills, hooks and settings for the repository.
Lifecycle shell scripts in .openhands/hooks.json: block dangerous commands, enforce quality checks before stopping, inject context.
Bundles of skills, hooks, MCP servers, agents and commands in reusable packages; portable Agent Plugins format works across compatible clients; browsable in Agent Canvas.
Model Context Protocol support lets OpenHands use external tool servers for custom tools and data sources.
Scheduled AI-powered tasks (cron) that each run a full OpenHands conversation, plus event-based triggers from custom webhooks (e.g. Linear).
Ready-made automations: issue-to-PR, GitHub PR review assistant, GitHub repository monitor and Slack channel monitor.
Register custom webhook event sources under Automate then Events and trigger automations from them.
Back up, share and edit Agent Canvas automations through a git repository.
Work with conversations including branching from previous messages; per-conversation agent profile and LLM profile.
Branch off an existing conversation for follow-up exploration without contaminating the original.
Pause agent execution and resume without losing state; interrupt a running agent with additional context or corrections.
Opt-in two-tier memory that survives across conversations (root causes, environment quirks, project decisions).
Condense conversation history to manage agent memory and save tokens.
Delegate complex work to specialized sub-agents that run synchronously and return results to the parent.
Define specialized sub-agents as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, no Python required.
Run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi or OpenCode inside Agent Canvas via the Agent Client Protocol.
Reusable agent configurations for Canvas conversations.
LLM-based critic evaluates agent actions with built-in iterative refinement.
Add trusted custom pages and integrated tools to Agent Canvas without forking the app.
Access Agent Canvas from mobile devices via Tailscale or ngrok.
Python SDK for building software agents: built-in and custom tools, structured output, parallel tool execution, metrics and OpenTelemetry tracing.
Remote agent execution exposing conversations, tools and workspaces over REST and WebSocket APIs, with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint mode.
Detect and handle stuck agents automatically with timeout mechanisms.
Let an agent consult a saved Oracle LLM profile for stateless second-opinion advice.
User-modeling agent that personalizes guidance based on inferred intent and preferences.
Agents interact with terminal applications like ipython and other interactive CLIs.
Provide environment variables and secrets to agent workspaces securely.
Send images to multimodal agents for vision-based tasks.
Repo spans Agent Canvas, Software Agent SDK, Agent Server, Automation Server, Sandbox Server and docs, plus OpenHands Enterprise for licensed self-hosting or managed deployment.
